app.Response.description: The Response struct is used for wrapping the API response with a code, message, and data.

code.description:
Code is the HTTP status code or a custom code used to indicate the result of the request
@example 200

data.description:
Data is the response data (can be any object or null)
@example {"id": 1, "name": "John Doe"}

msg.description:
Msg is the message that describes the result of the request
@example "Request successful"

info.description: Crawlora is a hosted web-data and SERP API: call documented REST endpoints and get normalized JSON instead of HTML to parse — across search/SERP, maps and local, e-commerce, app stores, social, media and finance. One API key; Crawlora runs the proxy rotation, headless browsers and parsing behind the scenes. Billed pay-on-success: charged only on a successful 2xx response, 1-10 credits per call, with a free tier of 2,000 credits per month and no card. A hosted MCP server (mcp.crawlora.net/mcp) exposes the same catalog as agent tools. Search endpoints accept `q` as a universal alias for whichever search-term parameter they document (`query`, `term`, `keyword`, or Amazon's `k`), so one parameter name works across the whole catalog; an explicitly supplied documented name always wins.
info.title: Crawlora API

get.description: Returns the complete filter taxonomy for the Creative Center trend endpoints: the countries each trend tab reports, the industry ids and video content tags the filters accept, the supported lookback periods, and the video sort metrics. Use it to discover valid values for the hashtags endpoint's country_code, period, and industry_id parameters and the videos endpoint's country_code, period, sort_by, and content_label_ids parameters. This endpoint performs no upstream request and has no parameters.

get.description: Returns TikTok Creative Center's ranked trending hashtags for a country, period, and optional industry. TikTok gates this endpoint's full result set behind a logged-in TikTok One account: an anonymous request always receives at most 3 hashtags per filter combination regardless of country, period, or industry, so selecting an industry returns that industry's own ranked top three. See the filters endpoint for the complete country, period, and industry value lists.

get.description: Returns TikTok Creative Center's current Top Content set: four top-performing branded videos, each with the video object (anonymous MP4 and cover URLs), engagement metrics, the author profile and follower count, and (by default) the video's top comments plus keyword mention counts derived from them. The set is a daily snapshot and there is no pagination or historical query; the four titles rotate when the snapshot changes. Set include_comments=false for a smaller response with only video, author, and metrics.

parameters.description: Include each object's top comments and comment-keyword counts
parameters.name: include_comments

get.description: Returns TikTok Creative Center's ranked trending videos for a country, period, sort order, and optional content tags. TikTok reports the true result-set size (see total_count/page_count in the response) but gates access to it behind a logged-in TikTok One account: an anonymous request always receives page 1 (4 videos) regardless of sort order or period. Country coverage is uneven: only US, JP, ID, VN, and TH have a regional edge host that returns populated results; other countries return an empty videos array (a genuine no-data response, not an error). See the filters endpoint for the complete country, period, sort, and content tag value lists.

get.description: Calls the app's primary feed route - `POST /aweme/v2/feed/`, which the Android client sends with a protobuf request body and answers with protobuf - and returns a schema-free decode: field numbers become keys, length-delimited fields become strings when printable, nested messages when they parse and base64 otherwise, plus a flat list of every string leaf. Field numbering is inferred because TikTok publishes no schema for this message; use the JSON `GET /tiktok/mobile/feed` route when you need the stable structured contract.
get.summary: Fetch the app's primary feed call (POST, protobuf) decoded without a schema

get.description: Returns one hashtag's detail by name: `challenge_info` (cid, hashtag_name, desc, ...) and `stats` (view and video counts), exactly as the mobile API returns them. Hashtags are addressed by name; an internal id is rejected upstream.

Lists videos for one hashtag name as the mobile app returns them (`aweme_list` with author, music and statistics), plus `cursor` and `has_more`. `sort=fresh` is the newest list and works from any measured egress; `sort=popular` is the hot list and only answers from a US egress.

There are no request parameters and no paging, and the body is large because the catalogue is complete.

Returns the complete LIVE gift catalogue in one call: `data.gifts` (771 gift objects with `diamond_count`, `describe`, `duration`, `gift_resources`, `gift_skins`, `batch_gift_info` and `combo`) plus the gift config and resource maps (`gift_configs`, `gifts_info`, `doodle_templates`, `gift_name_group_map`, `gift_resource_group_map`). There are no request parameters and no paging: the response is a single complete catalogue.

Searches the mobile app's LIVE surface by keyword: `data` of `{type, anchor}` entries with `feedback_type` set to `live`, plus `cursor` and `has_more`. `keyword` is required; without it the gateway answers a valid but empty envelope. This is the API's first LIVE endpoint.
